newsitem.title: CHINA: NON-STOP HK-MINNEAPOLIS NORTHWEST FLIGHT FOR OCT.
newsitem.headline: NON-STOP HK-MINNEAPOLIS NORTHWEST FLIGHT FOR OCT.

text.p: Northwest Airlines has received government approval to start a three times a week, non-stop passenger service from Hong Kong to Minneapolis/St Paul from October 2, the airline's Hong Kong manager Gilbert Chow said.

The Boeing 747-400 flight will also offer additional trans-Pacific cargo capacity to the U.S. midwest, but due to the distance and year-round weather conditions, belly cargo space may be limited, he told Reuters.

"Primarily the new service is passenger focused but there are definitely cargo opportunities from Hong Kong, although they may not be that great. We will need the experience of operating the route. The more cargo we can get on the aircraft the better the final bottom line will be," Chow added.

If wind conditions force Northwest to take-off over densely crowded Kowlonn, flights from Kai Tak may not be able to carry any cargo. However uplift capability is expected to improve substantially when Hong Kong's new airport opens next year, Chow added.
Northwest said the new service of around 14 hours 30 minutes from Hong Kong and an hour longer westbound will offer the fastest year round service between Hong Kong and many U.S. cities.
The airline offers more than 400 flights a day from from Minneapolis/St Paul hub, more than half of the them to midwest and east coast destinations.

The additional capacity to the U.S. midwest will compete with Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd 's newly restarted freighter service to Chicago and United Airlines Boeing 747-400 passenger service from Hong Kong to Chicago, although the latter only operates during the summer.
